Class 3 · Chapter 5 of 10

Read scales and change units

Read scales on rulers and thermometers, compare mass and capacity, and change units.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Shapes, reflections and boundaries. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can read a ruler or thermometer.
  • I can compare mass and capacity.
  • I can combine mixed units.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Read the scale

Before you read, find how much each small step is worth.

Here the labels are 10 apart and each tick is 1. The marker shows 35.

Screen 2 of 5

Read a thermometer

A thermometer is a scale you read upwards. Higher means hotter.

The reading is 28 degrees Celsius.

Screen 3 of 5

Compare mass

A balance shows which object has more mass.

The right side is lower, so it is heavier. Add to the left to level it.

Screen 4 of 5

Compare capacity

Capacity is how much a container holds, in litres or millilitres.

Jug B holds 5 litres. Jug A holds 3 litres.

Screen 5 of 5

Change units first

Only add numbers when the units match. 1 kg is 1000 g.

1 kg 500 g is 1000 g + 500 g = 1500 g.

Words to know
scale
The marked numbers on a ruler, jug or thermometer.
interval
How much one small step on a scale is worth.
mass
How much matter an object has. We measure it in g and kg.

For parents

What your child learns

Use the same unit before you add or subtract. 1 kg is 1000 g and 1 km is 1000 m. For a trail, find the distance between two points by subtracting their positions.

A common slip

Children may subtract numbers with different units. Change them to the same unit first. Then check the size: a watermelon is about kilograms, not grams.

5-minute home activity: Weigh and compare

  1. Weigh two packets on a kitchen scale if you have one.
  2. Write each weight in grams.
  3. Find how many grams heavier one is.
  4. Draw a trail with distances and find the gap between two stops.
